title: Every night on my drive home, a radio station I can't find in daylight reads the traffic. Tonight it described my car.
story:
It comes in around mile marker thirty, on the empty stretch between the gas station and my exit. Just static, then a calm man reading traffic. No music, no ads, no station name.

The reports were boring at first. A stalled truck. Fog near the river. I tried to find the station on my lunch break once. Nothing on that frequency but hiss.

Then last week he said, "A silver hatchback heading north. One driver. Drive safe." I drive a silver hatchback. I was the only car on the road.

The next night he said the hatchback's left taillight was out. I checked when I got home. It was.

Two nights ago, he said, "Silver hatchback, northbound. One driver, one passenger." I was alone. I said it out loud, just to hear myself. I'm alone.

Tonight, at mile marker thirty, the static cleared, and he sounded closer than ever, like he was sitting in the back seat.

"Silver hatchback, northbound. The passenger has asked the driver not to check the mirror. The driver is doing very well."

I've got four miles to my exit. The radio is off. The back seat creaked a minute ago, the way it does when someone leans forward.

I haven't looked.
premise: late-night radio traffic report tracks the narrator's car and then reports a passenger who asks the driver not to check the mirror
